# Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant

Official code for the accepted 2026 Transactions on Machine Learning Research
paper “Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output
Divergence in LLM Inference.”

The work shows that BF16 and FP16 greedy decoding can produce different LLM
outputs even with the same model, prompt, hardware, and decoding algorithm. It
studies top-two logit margins and selective FP32 output-head recomputation.

## Canonical links

- Paper: https://openreview.net/forum?id=QDOKyg7a5e
- PDF: https://openreview.net/pdf?id=QDOKyg7a5e
- Code: https://github.com/Hiramdu/greedy-decoding-cross-precision-divergence
- TMLR index: https://jmlr.org/tmlr/papers/

## Repository map

- README.md: project overview, results, setup, and usage
- run_core_experiment.py: BF16/FP16 baseline and Intervention C experiment
- requirements.txt: Python dependencies
- paper.bib: canonical TMLR BibTeX
- CITATION.cff: GitHub citation metadata
- codemeta.json: structured software metadata

## Search concepts

LLM inference, greedy decoding, numerical precision, BF16, FP16, FP32,
cross-precision output divergence, top-two logit margin, deterministic
decoding, reproducibility, selective lm_head recomputation.
